# Setting Up Pictures and Files in Customer Messages

Once your lab can already text and email customers from OrderHub, one more step switches on picture and file messaging. This article covers that step and a couple of quick checks. For what customers actually receive, see **Sending Pictures and Files to Customers**.

---

## What you don't need

* **No S3 storage.** Pictures and files you send, and pictures customers text back, are stored securely by OrderHub. You don't need to set up your own storage.
* **No extra charge from OrderHub.** Picture messages are billed by Twilio on your own Twilio account, like normal texts.

---

## Step 1: Move your number to Pixfizz Conversations

Pictures only arrive as real picture messages (MMS) once your texting number is on Pixfizz Conversations. Until then, everything you send goes as a secure link.

1. Go to **Settings → Organization → Notify → SMS / RCS**.
2. Click **Verify credentials** to check your Twilio details are working.
3. In the **Conversations** section, click **Provision Conversations Service**.
4. Once it shows as provisioned, click **Enable Conversations inbound** and confirm.
   * Note: this saves your current incoming-text setting first. **Disable Conversations inbound** puts it back exactly as it was.
   * Note: if you'd rather not do this yourself, contact Pixfizz Support and we'll do it for you.



---

## Step 2: Check your numbers are assigned to brands

Your numbers should already be linked to your brands from when texting was set up. Just check:

1. In **Settings → Organization → Notify → SMS / RCS**, find **Numbers & brands**.
2. Make sure each texting number is assigned to the brand it belongs to.
   * Note: file links include your brand name, so customers can see who sent them. When a message has no order, staff are asked **"Which brand is this file from?"** before sending. Labs with a single brand never see this question.



---

## If customer pictures don't show up

Twilio keys are normally allowed to read pictures, so most labs never need this. If customers text you a picture and it doesn't appear in Messages, your Twilio key is probably restricted:

1. In Twilio, create a **Main** API key, or a restricted key that is allowed to read messages and message media.
2. Enter it under **Twilio API Key SID (recommended)** and **Twilio API Key Secret**, then click **Verify credentials**.

---

## Good to know

| Sending to | What the customer gets |
| --- | --- |
| US/Canada mobile | The first picture as a real picture message; any other files as links |
| UK and other countries | A secure link |
| Any PDF or document | A secure link |
| Email | A secure link |

* Links last **30 days**. After that the customer sees that the link has expired, but the file stays in the conversation for your staff.
* Up to **5 files** per message, **10 MB** each. Large pictures are shrunk automatically so they go through.
* Before sending picture messages to real customers, turn on **SMS Pumping Protection** and check **SMS Geo Permissions** in your Twilio account.
